This revival of Eugene O'Neill's masterpiece is anchored by Jessica Lange's powerhouse performance as the morphine-addicted Mary Tyrone, delivering a haunting portrayal that's both heartbreaking and mesmerizing.

This production of Long Day’s Journey Into Night, under the very tight direction of Jonathan Kent, with an atmospheric set by Tom Pye that allows the New England fog to affect your mood, will send you out into the night after a nourishing and provocative theatrical experience.
Overall, 'Long Day's Journey Into Night' is a masterpiece which should be seen and will hold your attention throughout the night.
This production of Long Day's Journey Into Night is a masterclass in acting, with Jessica Lange delivering a powerhouse performance that anchors the entire evening.
She is mesmerizing, and definitely the reason to see this play, rather than read it.
The actors are committed (if occasionally too actorly) and Jessica effectively captures the woman's isolation, loneliness, and regret.
If you have fond memories of an earlier production, treasure them and sit this one out.
Perhaps more fitting as a vintage peep show, than a well executed play, this Long Day’s Journey Into Night, sure makes one crave for the morrow.
You’ve not truly seen Jessica Lange perform until you catch Roundabout’s revival of Eugene O’Neill’s Long Day’s Journey Into Night— for this is probably her best performance in years, if not ever.

cn.t: Critics praise Jessica Lange's powerful performance in this well-acted revival, though opinions split on Jonathan Kent's direction. Some find it riveting and immaculately paced, while others criticize it as static and overly long.
